Slovakia’s Poss-SLPC sro Reports Stable Steel Trade Figures in Latest Update

Bratislava, June 19 – Slovak steelmaker Poss-SLPC sro reported routine trade figures for the past quarter, with shipments and production levels holding steady amid stable demand from domestic and regional clients, according to a company statement released Wednesday.

The Bratislava-based firm, a key supplier to construction and engineering firms in Central Europe, said total steel output in the first quarter reached 178,000 tonnes, in line with the previous quarter and up 2% from the same period last year. Export volumes remained consistent, with the company shipping 74,500 tonnes to neighboring countries, including the Czech Republic, Hungary, and Austria.

“Market conditions have remained relatively steady, and we continue to see reliable demand from our core customers,” said Ján Král, commercial director at Poss-SLPC sro. “Our order book for the coming months looks healthy and we are on track to meet our annual targets.”

The Slovak Steel Association noted that the figures reflect a broader period of stability in the sector following a year of moderate growth and improved supply chain reliability. “Steelmakers have benefited from stabilized energy prices and restored logistics networks, allowing for smoother operations,” said association spokesperson Petra Hlinková.

Industry analysts pointed to ongoing investment in infrastructure projects and automotive components as helping to support steel demand in the region. “We expect Slovak steel producers to maintain output levels through the summer, barring any unforeseen external shocks,” said Tomáš Urban, an analyst with Central Europe Metals Review.

Poss-SLPC sro reported no production disruptions or significant changes in its workforce, which stands at approximately 620 employees. The company said it continues to monitor market conditions but does not anticipate any major changes to its operations in the near term.
